Class IncrementalECPartition

java.lang.Object
org.iam.core.IncrementalECPartition
@ParametersAreNonnullByDefault public class IncrementalECPartition extends Object
Technique 1 of the paper: the equivalence class (EC) partitioning of one domain, plus the bookkeeping that lets a later mining task reuse it instead of rebuilding.

The state is a partition of the domain's semantic space into mutually disjoint OperableLabel regions (the "atoms" / ECs), each associated with the set of labels covering it, together with the mapping M from each label to the ECs it covers. A new mining task hands in its full label set through update(Set):

  • a variable whose label set has not changed is unaffected, and its partition is kept as it is — no EC is recomputed;
  • for an affected variable, only the newly added labels are absorbed, and each of them splits just the existing ECs that have a non-empty intersection with it. An EC with an empty intersection is left untouched, index included (Delta-net's atom-splitting).

Persistent EC indices. Each unique EC gets an index that is never reused: the ECs a split removes have their indices abandoned rather than reassigned, so the indices of the ECs that survive an update stay valid across successive mining tasks.

Since:
2026-10-09

    • update

      public IncrementalECPartition.Update update(Set<Label> currentLabels)
      Absorbs the label set of the current mining task.

      Labels already processed are skipped, so a domain whose label set did not change is reported as unaffected and its partition is left exactly as it was.

      Parameters:
      currentLabels - the full label set of the current mining task
      Returns:
      what this update did
